To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a ZnO overlaid microstructured optical fibre is capable of optofluidics switching.
We have demonstrated the development of an optofluidically switchable microstructured optical fiber, based on a ZnO nanocoating.
we demonstrate the development of a light driven optofluids switch, based on a ZnO-overlayed MOF.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a light driven optofluids switching device, in the form of a ZnO-overlayered MOF Fabry–Perot interferometer, with the potential to be integrated in a wide range of photonic devices and systems, for the purpose of controlling and sensing fluidic processes.
the development of light triggered smart in-fiber optical microfluidic devices, suitable for sensing and actuation applications.
the development of a novel ZnO-overlapped MOF Fabry Perot cavity, with a fully reversible optofuidic switching behaviour, which is entirely based on UV and green light actuation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented study is the first to demonstrate light triggered reversible optofluids switching in a MOF Fabry Perot interferometer.
a light driven optofluids switch has been demonstrated.

a ZnO-overlaied MOF Fabry Perot interferometer has been demonstrated, with its optofluidics switching behaviour being fully reversible and light triggered, with UV 248 nm laser and green 532nm laser being employed as light sources.

the light triggered optofluidics is a new field that has been recently emerged and is very promising.
the light triggered optofluidics in the ZnO-overladed MOF is based on a light triggered wicking phenomenon.
the developed optofluidically switchable ZnO-MOF Fabry-PerOT can be used in the future for the development of novel optofluidics based sensors and switches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the light driven switching mechanism can be fully reversed and repeated several times, without the need of any external actuation, i.e. pressure or voltage, or chemical treatment.
the light-triggered switching of fluids in MOFs is possible, and the ZnO nanolayers are the ideal candidate for the fabrication of such optofluidics.
